news.title: Americans’ Use of Internet, Broadband in 2026
news.summary_en: The internet represents a fundamental shift in how Americans connect with one another, gather information and conduct their day-to-day lives. Explore the patterns, trends and statistics of internet and home broadband adoption in the United States.

news.title: Americans’ Use of Social Media in 2026
news.summary_en: Today YouTube and Facebook are the most-widely used online platforms. Explore the demographic patterns and trends shaping the social media landscape.

news.title: Americans’ Use of Mobile Devices in 2026
news.summary_en: Americans today are increasingly connected to the world of digital information while “on the go” via smartphones. Explore the latest patterns, trends and statistics that have shaped the mobile revolution.

news.title: 1 in 5 Americans Regularly Get News on TikTok
news.summary_en: Among adults under 30, 39% say they regularly get news from TikTok, up from 9% in 2020.

news.title: News Platform Fact Sheet
categories: State Of The News Media Project
news.summary_en: How Americans get news continues to evolve as platforms emerge, like AI chatbots and email newsletters. Find out how often they get news from digital devices.

news.title: Social Media and News Fact Sheet
news.summary_en: Many Americans use social media for news: About a fifth or more regularly get news on Facebook, YouTube, Instagram and TikTok.

news.title: How Latino Voters Are Experiencing the 2026 Midterm Elections
news.summary_en: Democratic congressional candidates have a sizable advantage among Latino registered voters. And Latino Democratic candidate supporters are more engaged with this year’s election compared with four years ago.

news.title: The Gender Gap in AI
news.summary_en: Men and women now use AI chatbots at similar rates, but men use them more often, while women are more skeptical of AI’s impact on their lives.

news.title: Republicans’ Views of Some Countries and International Organizations Differ Widely by Age
news.summary_en: Younger Republicans’ views of some countries and international organizations are sometimes closer to Democrats’ views than they are to those of older Republicans.

news.title: How Do Americans Feel About G20 Countries?
news.summary_en: Ahead of this year’s G20 summit, most Americans rate Australia, Canada, Japan, Italy and other members warmly. Sentiment is coldest toward Russia.
